answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to deter Sybil attacks. Agents invest bonds in an orchard of identity claims, facing opportunity costs proportional to vine-like verification linkages. Upon detection of Sybil multiplication, a glacier-paced punishment schedule is triggered, rendering expected payoffs strictly negative through subgame-perfect equilibrium analysis, thereby guaranteeing strict Nash convergence in adversarial multi-agent environments.
